title: lanes/spec.md: the landed ledger-append pre-approval states the permission but not the test — the case that grew a closed vocabulary is the one it does not answer
body:
Filed unassigned by the skills seat (`session_01RMTpSRF5CjMmQBFfPtPCwJ`) while landing #11368, so the input does not disappear when that card closes. **Record, not a claim; no grading here** — no `pm:queue`, no priority.

## Where it comes from

The engine seat left a data point on #11368 (comment of 2026-08-23T18:11Z) that #11368's own scope could not absorb. #11368 is a *recording* card: the spec seat ruled "pre-approved as a class, three conditions" on its seat post, and the card's job was to write that ruling into `references/lanes/spec.md`. It has now landed (branch `claude/issue-11368-lanes-facts`).

The engine seat's point is that the ruling as written answers one of the two cases a seat actually meets:

- **Case A — a genuinely new code, gate-mandated append.** Answered by the landed line: pre-approved, three conditions, spec-seat card outside the class.
- **Case B — same defect family, no new code.** A seat found that reusing an existing member with a second message composer (widening that entry's *comment* only) was the better shape, because both spellings say the same thing to a consumer and neither buys it a branch it could act on differently. ADR-0112 D3/D4 keep the `code` vocabulary closed and require exhaustive switching; D2's 2026-08-18 amendment retired three members precisely because an unreachable-or-redundant entry teaches a branch that carries no information.

Case B is where a seat is most likely to guess, because the cheap move — append a code — is also the move that grows a closed vocabulary. The landed text is silent on it.

## The suggestion, restated

Whatever the lane file says would be more useful if it also stated the **test** the two cases actually turned on: *does this defect give a consumer a branch it could act on differently?* — not only the permission to append.

## Why it was not folded into #11368

Writing that test into the lane file would **extend** the spec seat's ruling, not record it. The spec seat ruled on the permission boundary; nobody has ruled on the vocabulary-growth test. A dev seat adding it in passing would be inventing a second criterion inside a governed instruction file — exactly what the lane files exist to prevent.

## Cost note for whoever triages this

`references/lanes/spec.md` is at its ratchet ceiling (46 lines, headroom 0). Anything added there is paid for by compression in the same file, so this is not a free one-liner; it may also be a better fit for the ADR-0112 material than for the lane file. Both halves are a judgement for the spec seat / the maintainer, not for the seat filing this.
